newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mall group sees holiday sales up 4 to 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mall group sees holiday sales up 4 to 5 pct.

text.p: Sales at U.S. regional malls for the first 10 days of the holiday shopping season remain on target for a projected increase of between four percent and five percent over last year's holidays, the International Council of Shopping Centers said on Tuesday.
The council said sales in the malls surveyed in its study from Friday, November 29 through Sunday, December 8 are up 17.4 percent, compared with the first 10 days after Thanksgiving last year.
However, the double-digit increase was expected early in the season because this year there are five fewer days between Thanksgiving and Christmas than there were in 1995, the study said.

As the five fewer days are reflected in the shopping period, the gains are expected to slip to the four to five percent range, Hohn Konarski, the trade group's vice president of research, said in a statement.
The council's database of 62 malls measures sales per square foot in more than 3,300 specialty stores, but it does not include department stores and other mall "anchors," the group said.
The council will be reporting weekly holiday sales figures from this database through December 26, 1996, it said.
